newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mixed but hovers near record highs.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed but hovers near record highs.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were narrowly mixed in quiet trade on Monday after the market's stellar performance last week pushed prices to record highs, Brady bond experts said.

"We have seen some profit-taking across the board this morning but nothing dramatic and I would say the real direction will come from New York. The market is not sure what to do here because purely on a price basis we are at highest we have been ever," a Brady trader at a European bank in London said.
Experts said a sharp rally in U.S. Treasuries on Friday, coupled with improving fundamentals among emerging market countries have contributed to the significant price gains.

Still, market experts said the emerging debt market will continue to monitor U.S. economic data in coming weeks in order to better gauge what the Federal Reserve's next move might be on U.S. monetary policy.
The Fed's policy-setting body, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), will next meet to deliberate on interest rate levels on July 1 and July 2.

"There is a real difference of opinion on what is going to happen (at the FOMC) in July so although everybody said the unemployment numbers were going to be the last key number, I think people will be really be staring at the next few," a Brady bond trader said.
Data to be released later in the week includes May U.S. retail sales on Thursday and May U.S. producer prices on Friday.
Meanwhile, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans, which have been among the top performers, were unchanged at 89-1/2 bid, just below its record highs of 89-5/8 reached on Friday.
Market specialists attributed the price gains on Russian loans to continued progress in the reconciliation of its debt owed to its commercial bank creditors.

Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters in Moscow on Sunday that the country would set a date for signing the rescheduling agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors in July.
"By the end of June or start of July, Vneshekonombank will finish reconciling the remaining sum and then we can count on creditors approving the remaining sum during July," he said.
"By mid-July there will come a moment when we shall have every reason to set the signing date so that the exact closing date can be calculated," he added.
Among the Latin Brady instruments, prices were narrowly mixed in quiet trade.
Venezuelan FLIRBS VZ6C97=RR were 1/4 firmer at 92-1/4 bid after posting sharp gains last week on news of the country's upgrade by Standard and Poor's Corp.

In addition, Venezuelan Brady instruments stregnthened on comments by the energy minister on Friday, who suggested that the country use the $2.17 billion bid for 18 oil field operating contracts to pay off debt.

"We (the ministry) are responsible for generating these revenues, and not their application... But I agree with PDVSA's president that the funds be used to amortize debt and meet service payments," Venezuelan Minister of Energy and Mines Erwin Arrieta told reporters in Caracas on Friday.

Elsewhere, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/4 weaker at 80-3/8 bid on profit-taking after scoring sharp gains on the success of its $3.0 billion global bond issue and the passage of the re-election amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term.
"It's all hunky dory at the moment," said Peter West, director of emerging markets at West Merchant Bank, who cited the positive news on Brazil, Russia and Venezuela.
"Our index is at its highest level ever, exceeding the previous high on February 25," West added.
--Diane Craft, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5110
